title: Accept and enforce the DG-01 rendering topology
outcome: Accepted architecture contracts and one deterministic successor check consistently require a private production/test Astro renderer for exactly the cataloged on-demand routes, gateway-served static output, a separately private API, and gateway-only public exposure, while rejecting every renderer-route or public-reachability declaration outside the complete canonical sections.
scope: Record the approved DG-01 private Astro renderer direction in AGENTS.md and the synchronized accepted ADR, technology, Compose, configuration, and observability contracts, reconciled onto the exact main base without importing blocked-ticket history.

Require the gateway to serve static, prerendered, and fingerprinted output, route exactly the page catalog's five on-demand patterns to private web, route /api/v1/* to the separately private Deno API, and remain the only production-like host-exposed service.

Constrain web to generated API contracts, a private API origin, forwarded request context, and renderer operations configuration without database, object-store, provider, identity-key, backend-internal, or direct-adapter authority; define renderer readiness, correlation, redaction, and cache boundaries.

Add one successor-named, self-contained built-in-Deno architecture contract check whose in-memory discriminators parse the complete unique Gateway Routing section, structurally allowlist the complete unique Network Exposure section, and validate the authoritative contracts against the unchanged page catalog.
nonGoals: Declare blocked FND-001, FND-002, or PRODUCT-001 as a dependency; accept, alter, merge, cherry-pick, or copy the blocked FND-001 packet or lineage; or modify docs/planning/tickets/FND-001.

Implement or configure the Astro renderer, gateway, Docker Compose stack, application scaffold, health endpoints, images, dependencies, root manifests or locks, hooks, deployment, or runtime behavior.

Change the page catalog, product catalogs or routes, schema bundle, module boundaries, authorization matrix, ADR index, planning proposals, root task definitions, .codex, .agents, or unrelated documentation.

Select or pin the DG-12 gateway product, routing/config generator, security headers, forwarding implementation, TLS approach, Astro adapter, Node version, package manager, telemetry provider, ingress, or deployment provider.
Push, deploy, integrate, merge into main, create integration.md, or claim the later production-image and end-to-end implementation proof.

acceptanceCriteria.text: ADR 0001, AGENTS.md, the technology baseline, and the Compose contract consistently require a private Astro runtime in production and test for exactly the five on-demand page-catalog ID/path pairs; the gateway serves static and prerendered output, routes /api/v1/* to the private Deno API, remains the only public service, and development alone overrides web to astro dev.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: deno test --allow-read=AGENTS.md,docs/architecture/decisions/0001-astro-personalized-rendering.md,docs/architecture/technology-baseline.md,docs/architecture/compose-contract.md,docs/architecture/configuration-and-secrets.md,docs/architecture/observability.md,docs/product/page-catalog.yaml tools/architecture/FND-001S/astro_rendering_topology_contract_test.ts fails against unchanged contracts only because the accepted private-renderer topology is absent; its in-memory route discriminator first proves that the exact canonical section passes and contiguous extra, separated extra, later contradictory prose, second route table, missing, duplicate, and malformed variants each fail.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The accepted configuration and dependency boundary permits web to use only generated API contracts, a private API origin, forwarded request context, and renderer operations configuration, and forbids database, object-store, provider, identity-key, backend-internal, and direct-adapter authority.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The same focused Deno command fails its authoritative repository assertion against the byte-unchanged baseline because the accepted configuration and technology contracts do not yet define the private renderer's exact capability boundary, while the in-memory discriminator self-tests pass.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The accepted Compose and observability contracts require private renderer liveness/readiness, bounded gateway dependency behavior, gateway-to-web-to-API correlation, safe route templates, token and query redaction, non-cacheable personalized responses, and cacheable fingerprinted static assets without claiming runtime implementation.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The same focused Deno command fails its authoritative repository assertion against the byte-unchanged baseline because renderer readiness, correlation, redaction, and personalized-response cache rules are absent, while all in-memory lifecycle and text discriminators pass.

acceptanceCriteria.text: One frozen successor architecture check derives the exact on-demand set from the unchanged page catalog, validates the real accepted contracts, bounds inputs, rejects missing, duplicate, malformed, broadened, contradictory, and noncanonical complete-section shapes, structurally allowlists complete Network Exposure claims, and achieves exactly 100 percent line, branch, and function coverage without weakening its frozen bytes during GREEN.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The focused Deno test and an exact-threshold Deno coverage command prove all in-memory route and exposure discriminators before contract edits; only the authoritative repository assertion is RED, and the controller freezes the single test/check file plus its lowercase SHA-256 before GREEN.

risks: A parser that stops at the first non-table line could ignore a separated row, later renderer-route prose, or a second route table and let gateway-to-web routing broaden beyond the catalog while enforcement remains green.
A vocabulary blacklist for public exposure could miss a synonym or malformed claim and permit web, API, or a data service to become publicly reachable without deterministic rejection.
A server-side Astro runtime could receive database, provider, object-store, or identity-key authority or import backend internals unless the contract and check are explicit.
Verification, reset, invitation, MFA, cookie, and compliance data could leak through raw URLs, logs, traces, metrics, caches, or error artifacts.
Harvesting a broad predecessor diff could delete or rewrite integrated FND-002 or PRODUCT-001 work because the predecessor candidate diverges before the current main base.
Broad wording could silently preselect the still-open DG-12 gateway, TLS, forwarding, security-header, or configuration-generation choice reserved for a separate ticket.
